title: Sensex, Nifty Reverse Intraday Losses to Close Higher as Crude Oil Falls 3%
excerpt: Indian benchmarks recovered from early-session weakness as oil dropped to a one-week low, while the first monthly Nifty derivatives expiry under the new closing auction system drove sharp late-session swings.
body:
• Sensex closed at 77,656, up 287 points (0.37%), while Nifty gained 116 points (0.48%) to 24,335 after trading lower for most of the session.
  • Brent crude fell 3.2% to $89.20 per barrel as traders shrugged off the latest U.S. sanctions campaign against Iran.
  • Tuesday marked the first monthly Nifty 50 derivatives expiry under the new closing auction system, driving sharp price swings in the final trading hour.
  • Twelve of 16 major sectors closed higher, with IT stocks leading gains at 0.6% and financials rising 0.3%.

Indian equity benchmarks reversed a choppy, largely negative session on Tuesday to close with solid gains, as a sharp drop in crude oil prices and derivatives expiry-related positioning drove a late-hour rally.

The BSE Sensex ended at 77,656.09, up 286.98 points or 0.37%, while the Nifty 50 settled at 24,334.55, gaining 115.50 points or 0.48%. Both indices had spent most of the day in negative territory — the Sensex was down more than 200 points at midday, and the Nifty had dipped below 24,150 — before reversing course in the final hour of trade.

Oil Drop Shifts Sentiment

The catalyst for the turnaround was a 3.2% slide in Brent crude to $89.20 per barrel, its lowest level in a week. Traders shrugged off the latest round of U.S. economic sanctions against Iran, betting that Washington’s preference for economic pressure over military escalation reduces the immediate risk of a supply disruption from the Gulf.

Oil prices had been a persistent headwind for Indian equities. The Nifty logged seven consecutive losing sessions through last Wednesday — its longest streak in 11 months — as Brent held above $92 and global bond yields climbed to multi-decade highs. Tuesday’s crude pullback offered the first sustained relief in over a week.

Derivatives Expiry Amplifies Swings

Tuesday also marked the first monthly Nifty 50 derivatives expiry under the exchange’s new closing auction system (CAS), adding an extra layer of volatility to an already uncertain session.

“Monthly expiry-related rollovers and positioning led to sharper-than-usual price swings, particularly during the final hour of trading.”

— Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, CEO, HST Wealth

The CAS mechanism, introduced earlier this month, has already raised questions among market participants. An August 3 session saw a notable gap between the regular close and the auction-determined close, unsettling some traders. Rajesh Singla, CEO at Alpha AMC and Planify, noted that “the real test will be the next MSCI rebalancing on August 31.”

Sectors and Movers

Twelve of 16 major sectors logged gains. Information technology stocks led the advance, rising 0.6% after a bruising three-session selloff that had wiped out 4%. Heavyweight financials gained 0.3%, with both sectors reversing losses in the final hour.

Mid-cap stocks gained 0.5%, while small-caps edged down 0.1%, suggesting the rally was concentrated in larger names rather than a broad-based risk-on move.

Hindustan Copper was the session’s biggest laggard, falling 7.2% after the government announced plans to divest up to a 6% stake at a 10.5% discount to the stock’s last closing price. Federal Bank dropped about 3% and Jana Small Finance Bank fell 1.9% after CNBC-TV18 reported that Jana’s promoter may sell its entire 16.9% stake to Federal Bank. Federal Bank told exchanges there was no material event requiring disclosure.

On the upside, gold financiers Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance extended recent gains as gold prices held near three-month highs.

Macro Backdrop and Outlook

The broader context remains challenging. Indian benchmarks are down roughly 8–10% year-to-date, weighed by a record $25 billion in foreign fund outflows, elevated energy costs, and rising global bond yields. A weaker-than-expected monsoon — rainfall is forecast to end the season about 15% below the long-term average — adds domestic risk through potential food price inflation and subdued rural demand.

Foreign institutional investors turned net buyers on Monday, purchasing shares worth ₹1,182 crore, but sustained inflow momentum remains uncertain given the geopolitical overhang from the nearly six-month U.S.-Iran conflict.

Investors are now watching two near-term catalysts: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s address at the Jackson Hole Symposium later this week for signals on the U.S. rate path, and the MSCI rebalancing on August 31, which could trigger significant index-related flows into Indian equities.
